SQLite Datasources : Register SQLite databases programmatically or through minimal matchbox.toml datasource configuration. Inline CLI Execution : Execute source with --eval or -e , including prelude functions and source-located diagnostics. Changed dateFormat , timeFormat and dateTimeFormat now mirror BoxLang's DateTimeFormat BIF: masks are Java DateTimeFormatter patterns (case sensitive, mm is minutes, MM is month, invalid letters and repeat counts raise Java's errors), with Java's default masks, named masks ( short , medium , long , full , iso , iso8601 , odbc , javascript , epoch , epochms ), timezone and locale arguments and English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese, Dutch, Russian, Japanese and Chinese locale text. Locales without bundled data fall back to en_US ; named regions other than UTC/GMT use MatchBox's fixed-offset zone table (no tz database). createDateTime and createDate accept every argument as optional, like BoxLang ( createDateTime( 2024, 3, 5, 14, 7, 9 ) works, no arguments returns now). Fixed WASM time traps : The VM scheduler and getTickCount() now use web_time clocks; synchronous scheduler waits poll instead of calling unsupported std::thread::sleep in WASM builds. <bx:switch> evaluates its expression , runs only the matching <bx:case> (no fall-through, value with delimiters matches any listed item) and <bx:defaultcase> only when nothing matches; text after the switch is kept ( #93 ). super.method( args ) works in class methods: it calls the parent class implementation with this bound to the current instance, across any depth of inheritance and inside closures. Named arguments are not supported with super . new Child() calls init() inherited from a parent class when Child defines none (the compiler only looked at the class itself). --target wasi works again: the WASI runner stub lost its embed region in an earlier refactor, so packaging always failed with "WASI stub is missing the BOXLANG_EMBED sentinel". --target wasm produced an invalid module (a custom section written without its header) that no runtime could load; it is now the same as --target wasi . The docs said --target wasm was browser oriented; use --target js for the browser. Native Fusion reads native/Cargo.toml : its [dependencies] are added to the generated build (relative path dependencies are resolved against native/ ), as the Native Fusion guide already described. Redeclaring a crate the build provides ( matchbox_vm , postcard , bincode , anyhow ) is an error. Java interop ( bif-jni ): methods and constructors are chosen by their parameter types, not just argument count ( sb.append( 2 ) , String.valueOf( 5 ) ), static methods work on createObject( "java", ... ) references ( Math.max( 1, 2 ) , Integer.parseInt( "42" ) ), and Java exceptions report their class and message. for ( row in query ) iterates the rows of a query (it failed with "Iteration only supported for arrays and structs"). A BIF that is compiled out now says which build feature provides it, and the QoQ error names the qoq feature. Member functions that map to existing BIFs now resolve: struct keyArray , keyList , valueArray , filter , map , reduce , some , every , none , delete , insert , update , clear , copy , sort , findValue , hash ; string listToArray , listPrepend , listInsertAt , listSetAt , listReduce , jsonDeserialize , toBase64 , toBinary , yesNoFormat and other list/string members; array join , findNoCase , isDefined ; number max , min , formatBaseN ; date hash ; future isDone . Script lock name="x" timeout=n { ... } blocks parse and run their body (a lock never contends in the single-threaded VM). Script thread { ... } now parses and reports "The thread component is not supported yet in MatchBox" instead of a struct-literal parse error. Labeled loops: outer: for ( ... ) with continue outer / break outer (also while and do ) now work like BoxLang. Labels were parsed and silently ignored, so continue outer only continued the inner loop. The mod operator ( 7 mod 3 ) and unary not ( not x ) now parse, like BoxLang. mod stays usable as an identifier. private class methods are enforced: calling one from outside the class (or an unrelated class) throws, while calls from the class, its subclasses and its closures keep working. Class properties generate getX() / setX() by default ( accessors=false opts out), generated setters return the instance so calls chain, and obj.name / obj.name = v use the accessors when there is no such field, as in BoxLang. <bx:include template="..."> includes the named template instead of an empty path ( #93 ). class extends=Base implements=Speaker (and extends:Base ) accept an unquoted class name like BoxLang; only the quoted form parsed before. Script-level variables is now the same store as bare variables ( variables.k = 1; k and j = 2; variables.j work), and CLI scripts and class methods have a request scope. CLI argument handling now follows BoxLang's BoxRunner and CLIGetArgs : options only count before the script file, everything after it goes to the script ( matchbox app.bxs -v runs the script with -v ), -h / --help / -v / --version are global only as the sole argument, unknown options fall through like BoxLang, and cliGetArgs() parses --opt=value , --!opt / --no-opt , -o=value , -abc and quoted values exactly like BoxLang (a value is never taken from the next token) and keeps the first script argument. Breaking: put MatchBox options before the file ( matchbox --target esp32 --chip esp32s3 --flash app.bxs ); the documentation is updated, and the old -- separator is no longer special. Adds BoxLang's runtime flags: --bx-debug , --bx-code <code> , --bx-printAST (file, --bx-code or stdin) are implemented, --bx-config / --bx-home are accepted (never reach the script) with a warning that MatchBox ignores them, --bx-transpile is rejected clearly; and the server.cli scope ( args , parsed , executionPath , command ) with server.boxlang.cliMode . <bx:loop> works: from / to / step / index counting loops, array , list , collection and condition loops no longer run forever or print null ( #93 ). Security: ESP32 firmware no longer ships default Wi-Fi credentials. Without MATCHBOX_ESP32_WIFI_SSID / MATCHBOX_ESP32_WIFI_PASSWORD at build time Wi-Fi stays off and the boot log says so (the credentials that were in the source should be considered public). Destructuring rest elements ( [ a, ...rest ] = arr , { a, ...others } = struct ) are now assigned instead of silently dropped. arraySlice now follows BoxLang: start defaults to 1, length is a count (0 or omitted means to the end, negative trims from the end) and a negative start counts from the end. Calling a function without a required argument now throws Required argument [a] is missing for function [f] (type Application ) like BoxLang, instead of silently passing null. Tree-shaking no longer drops prelude functions that are only reached through member calls ( [3,1,2].sort() , .first() , .reverse() , .sum() , ... failed with "BIF arraysort not found" outside --no-shaking ). Removed prelude copies of abs , min , max , arrayIsEmpty , arrayPrepend , arrayContains and arrayContainsNoCase that shadowed the native BIFs depending on tree-shaking; arrayPrepend now returns the array and arrayContains is case-sensitive for arrays and case-aware for sets. Closures at script level can now see the for ( n in ... ) loop variable (and index) instead of failing with "Variable 'n' not found"; assignments to the loop variable in the body are shared with closures. future.get() inside a native callback ( map , filter , ...) no longer hangs: the nested callback now lets other fibers run while it waits. Array members map , each , filter , reduce , some , every and none no longer use the Set helpers: map kept only unique results, and callbacks now receive (value, index, array) ( (accumulator, value, index, array) for reduce ) like BoxLang. variables.n++ / ++variables.n inside classes and scripts no longer fail with "Fused increment only supported on structs and instances", and prefix ++ / -- now accept member targets such as ++s.n . new C() now evaluates to the instance when init() returns nothing or null , and to the returned value otherwise, matching BoxLang. Tree-shaking no longer drops prelude functions that are only reached through member calls ( [3,1,2].sort() , .first() , .reverse() , .sum() , ... failed with "BIF arraysort not found" outside --no-shaking ). Removed prelude copies of abs , min , max , arrayIsEmpty , arrayPrepend , arrayContains and arrayContainsNoCase that shadowed the native BIFs depending on tree-shaking; arrayPrepend now returns the array and arrayContains is case-sensitive for arrays and case-aware for sets. Corrected the native fusion documentation example that used the nonexistent BxValue::new_string ; strings are returned with BxValue::new_ptr( vm.string_new( text ) ) . Documentation Documented which BIF groups exist in WASM builds: hash() needs the bif-crypto feature, http() is not usable in the browser.

Released 2026-10-22. [GitHub release](https://github.com/ortus-boxlang/matchbox/releases/tag/v0.12.0) \| [Downloads](https://downloads.ortussolutions.com/ortussolutions/matchbox/0.12.0/)

## Added

* **HTML Encoding** : Added `encodeForHTML()` and its `htmlEditFormat()` alias, matching BoxLang JVM output.
* **SQLite Datasources** : Register SQLite databases programmatically or through minimal `matchbox.toml` datasource configuration.
* **Inline CLI Execution** : Execute source with `--eval` or `-e`, including prelude functions and source-located diagnostics.

## Changed

* `dateFormat`, `timeFormat` and `dateTimeFormat` now mirror BoxLang's `DateTimeFormat` BIF: masks are Java `DateTimeFormatter` patterns (case sensitive, `mm` is minutes, `MM` is month, invalid letters and repeat counts raise Java's errors), with Java's default masks, named masks (`short`, `medium`, `long`, `full`, `iso`, `iso8601`, `odbc`, `javascript`, `epoch`, `epochms`), `timezone` and `locale` arguments and English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese, Dutch, Russian, Japanese and Chinese locale text. Locales without bundled data fall back to `en_US`; named regions other than UTC/GMT use MatchBox's fixed-offset zone table (no tz database).
* `createDateTime` and `createDate` accept every argument as optional, like BoxLang (`createDateTime( 2024, 3, 5, 14, 7, 9 )` works, no arguments returns now).

## Fixed

* **WASM time traps** : The VM scheduler and `getTickCount()` now use `web_time` clocks; synchronous scheduler waits poll instead of calling unsupported `std::thread::sleep` in WASM builds.
* `<bx:switch>` evaluates its `expression`, runs only the matching `<bx:case>` (no fall-through, `value` with `delimiters` matches any listed item) and `<bx:defaultcase>` only when nothing matches; text after the switch is kept (`#93`).
* `super.method( args )` works in class methods: it calls the parent class implementation with `this` bound to the current instance, across any depth of inheritance and inside closures. Named arguments are not supported with `super`.
* `new Child()` calls `init()` inherited from a parent class when `Child` defines none (the compiler only looked at the class itself).
* `--target wasi` works again: the WASI runner stub lost its embed region in an earlier refactor, so packaging always failed with "WASI stub is missing the BOXLANG_EMBED sentinel". `--target wasm` produced an invalid module (a custom section written without its header) that no runtime could load; it is now the same as `--target wasi`. The docs said `--target wasm` was browser oriented; use `--target js` for the browser.
* Native Fusion reads `native/Cargo.toml`: its `[dependencies]` are added to the generated build (relative `path` dependencies are resolved against `native/`), as the Native Fusion guide already described. Redeclaring a crate the build provides (`matchbox_vm`, `postcard`, `bincode`, `anyhow`) is an error.
* Java interop (`bif-jni`): methods and constructors are chosen by their parameter types, not just argument count (`sb.append( 2 )`, `String.valueOf( 5 )`), static methods work on `createObject( "java", ... )` references (`Math.max( 1, 2 )`, `Integer.parseInt( "42" )`), and Java exceptions report their class and message.
* `for ( row in query )` iterates the rows of a query (it failed with "Iteration only supported for arrays and structs"). A BIF that is compiled out now says which build feature provides it, and the QoQ error names the `qoq` feature.
* Member functions that map to existing BIFs now resolve: struct `keyArray`, `keyList`, `valueArray`, `filter`, `map`, `reduce`, `some`, `every`, `none`, `delete`, `insert`, `update`, `clear`, `copy`, `sort`, `findValue`, `hash`; string `listToArray`, `listPrepend`, `listInsertAt`, `listSetAt`, `listReduce`, `jsonDeserialize`, `toBase64`, `toBinary`, `yesNoFormat` and other list/string members; array `join`, `findNoCase`, `isDefined`; number `max`, `min`, `formatBaseN`; date `hash`; future `isDone`.
* Script `lock name="x" timeout=n { ... }` blocks parse and run their body (a lock never contends in the single-threaded VM). Script `thread { ... }` now parses and reports "The thread component is not supported yet in MatchBox" instead of a struct-literal parse error.
* Labeled loops: `outer: for ( ... )` with `continue outer` / `break outer` (also `while` and `do`) now work like BoxLang. Labels were parsed and silently ignored, so `continue outer` only continued the inner loop.
* The `mod` operator (`7 mod 3`) and unary `not` (`not x`) now parse, like BoxLang. `mod` stays usable as an identifier.
* `private` class methods are enforced: calling one from outside the class (or an unrelated class) throws, while calls from the class, its subclasses and its closures keep working.
* Class properties generate `getX()`/`setX()` by default (`accessors=false` opts out), generated setters return the instance so calls chain, and `obj.name` / `obj.name = v` use the accessors when there is no such field, as in BoxLang.
* `<bx:include template="...">` includes the named template instead of an empty path (`#93`).
* `class extends=Base implements=Speaker` (and `extends:Base`) accept an unquoted class name like BoxLang; only the quoted form parsed before.
* Script-level `variables` is now the same store as bare variables (`variables.k = 1; k` and `j = 2; variables.j` work), and CLI scripts and class methods have a `request` scope.
* CLI argument handling now follows BoxLang's `BoxRunner` and `CLIGetArgs`: options only count before the script file, everything after it goes to the script (`matchbox app.bxs -v` runs the script with `-v`), `-h`/`--help`/`-v`/`--version` are global only as the sole argument, unknown options fall through like BoxLang, and `cliGetArgs()` parses `--opt=value`, `--!opt`/`--no-opt`, `-o=value`, `-abc` and quoted values exactly like BoxLang (a value is never taken from the next token) and keeps the first script argument. **Breaking:** put MatchBox options before the file (`matchbox --target esp32 --chip esp32s3 --flash app.bxs`); the documentation is updated, and the old `--` separator is no longer special. Adds BoxLang's runtime flags: `--bx-debug`, `--bx-code <code>`, `--bx-printAST` (file, `--bx-code` or stdin) are implemented, `--bx-config`/`--bx-home` are accepted (never reach the script) with a warning that MatchBox ignores them, `--bx-transpile` is rejected clearly; and the `server.cli` scope (`args`, `parsed`, `executionPath`, `command`) with `server.boxlang.cliMode`.
* `<bx:loop>` works: `from`/`to`/`step`/`index` counting loops, `array`, `list`, `collection` and `condition` loops no longer run forever or print `null` (`#93`).
* Security: ESP32 firmware no longer ships default Wi-Fi credentials. Without `MATCHBOX_ESP32_WIFI_SSID` / `MATCHBOX_ESP32_WIFI_PASSWORD` at build time Wi-Fi stays off and the boot log says so (the credentials that were in the source should be considered public).
* Destructuring rest elements (`[ a, ...rest ] = arr`, `{ a, ...others } = struct`) are now assigned instead of silently dropped.
* `arraySlice` now follows BoxLang: `start` defaults to 1, `length` is a count (0 or omitted means to the end, negative trims from the end) and a negative `start` counts from the end.
* Calling a function without a `required` argument now throws `Required argument [a] is missing for function [f]` (type `Application`) like BoxLang, instead of silently passing null.
* Tree-shaking no longer drops prelude functions that are only reached through member calls (`[3,1,2].sort()`, `.first()`, `.reverse()`, `.sum()`, ... failed with "BIF arraysort not found" outside `--no-shaking`).
* Removed prelude copies of `abs`, `min`, `max`, `arrayIsEmpty`, `arrayPrepend`, `arrayContains` and `arrayContainsNoCase` that shadowed the native BIFs depending on tree-shaking; `arrayPrepend` now returns the array and `arrayContains` is case-sensitive for arrays and case-aware for sets.
* Closures at script level can now see the `for ( n in ... )` loop variable (and index) instead of failing with "Variable 'n' not found"; assignments to the loop variable in the body are shared with closures.
* `future.get()` inside a native callback (`map`, `filter`, ...) no longer hangs: the nested callback now lets other fibers run while it waits.
* Array members `map`, `each`, `filter`, `reduce`, `some`, `every` and `none` no longer use the Set helpers: `map` kept only unique results, and callbacks now receive `(value, index, array)` (`(accumulator, value, index, array)` for `reduce`) like BoxLang.
* `variables.n++` / `++variables.n` inside classes and scripts no longer fail with "Fused increment only supported on structs and instances", and prefix `++`/`--` now accept member targets such as `++s.n`.
* `new C()` now evaluates to the instance when `init()` returns nothing or `null`, and to the returned value otherwise, matching BoxLang.
* Tree-shaking no longer drops prelude functions that are only reached through member calls (`[3,1,2].sort()`, `.first()`, `.reverse()`, `.sum()`, ... failed with "BIF arraysort not found" outside `--no-shaking`).
* Removed prelude copies of `abs`, `min`, `max`, `arrayIsEmpty`, `arrayPrepend`, `arrayContains` and `arrayContainsNoCase` that shadowed the native BIFs depending on tree-shaking; `arrayPrepend` now returns the array and `arrayContains` is case-sensitive for arrays and case-aware for sets.
* Corrected the native fusion documentation example that used the nonexistent `BxValue::new_string`; strings are returned with `BxValue::new_ptr( vm.string_new( text ) )`.

## Documentation

* Documented which BIF groups exist in WASM builds: `hash()` needs the `bif-crypto` feature, `http()` is not usable in the browser.

markdown:
Explore built-in functions and member methods by topic. These pages are generated from runtime registrations; availability depends on the target and build. For broader language documentation, see [BoxLang](https://boxlang.ortusbooks.com/).

## How to read the tables

|  Column  |                                                                                                                                    Meaning                                                                                                                                    |
|----------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Function | The function name. Member-only entries are written `type.name`.                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Forms    | How to call it. `name( ... )` is the global form and `type.name( ... )` is the member form on a value of that type, for example `string.ucase( ... )`. A literal `...` means the argument list is not recorded here. Functions written in BoxLang show their real parameters. |
| Gate     | `always`, or the cargo feature or crate that must be enabled for the function to exist.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Notes    | Behavior notes. Text appears only where it was checked against the source or by running MatchBox.                                                                                                                                                                             |

Function names are not case sensitive; the pages show the usual spelling.

## Pages

|                                        Page                                        | Entries | Member forms |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------|--------------|
| [Strings](/reference/functions/strings/index.html)                                 | 81      | 69           |
| [Arrays](/reference/functions/arrays/index.html)                                   | 72      | 56           |
| [Structs](/reference/functions/structs/index.html)                                 | 33      | 14           |
| [Numbers and Math](/reference/functions/numbers-and-math/index.html)               | 43      | 23           |
| [Dates and Time](/reference/functions/dates-and-time/index.html)                   | 47      | 57           |
| [Lists](/reference/functions/lists/index.html)                                     | 35      | 29           |
| [Queries and Datasources](/reference/functions/queries-and-datasources/index.html) | 43      | 1            |
| [Types and Decisions](/reference/functions/types-and-decisions/index.html)         | 36      | 16           |
| [System and CLI](/reference/functions/system-and-cli/index.html)                   | 50      |              |
| [Files and I/O](/reference/functions/files-and-io/index.html)                      | 44      |              |
| [JSON, YAML, TOML and XML](/reference/functions/data-formats/index.html)           | 27      | 15           |
| [Encoding and Crypto](/reference/functions/encoding-and-crypto/index.html)         | 18      | 4            |
| [Async and Futures](/reference/functions/async-and-futures/index.html)             | 28      | 11           |
| [Sets](/reference/functions/sets/index.html)                                       | 21      | 18           |
| [Cache and Watchers](/reference/functions/cache-and-watchers/index.html)           | 16      |              |
| [Locales and Currency](/reference/functions/i18n/index.html)                       | 13      | 1            |
| [HTTP and Network](/reference/functions/http/index.html)                           | 3       |              |
| [ESP32](/reference/functions/esp32/index.html)                                     | 29      |              |
| [Native Object Methods](/reference/functions/objects/index.html)                   | 226     |              |
| [Member functions](/reference/functions/members/index.html)                        | 314     |              |

## Counts

* Global functions: 610. 532 are native Rust functions, 55 are written in BoxLang (the prelude), 8 exist in both, 3 are handled by the compiler (println, print and echo; echo also exists as a native function) and 12 are TUI class names.
* ESP32 firmware functions: 29 (included in the global count above).
* Member functions on built-in types: 314.
* Native object methods: 226.
* Internal helper functions that only back the member table (`boxSet*`, `arrayAppendMember`) are not listed: 31.

## Feature gates

A gate names the build feature or runner a function needs. Features can also be enabled by dependencies; see [source builds](/getting-started/building-matchbox/index.html#cargo-features) for custom builds. The browser playground includes only `always` functions.

Other features change behavior without adding functions:

* `qoq` (not default): enables query of queries. `queryExecute` with `dbtype: "query"` returns the error "QoQ support is not enabled in this build" without it.
* `bif-jni` (default): `createObject( "java", ... )` creates Java objects. Without it the call fails with "Java interoperability is not enabled in this build."

## Not available in the browser playground

143 of the 610 global functions are not available in the playground build: the gated functions, including the ESP32 functions and the TUI classes. Common examples are `hash`, `encrypt`, `fileRead`, `directoryList`, `http`, `queryNew`, `queryExecute`, `cliRead` and `exit`. Member functions whose target function is gated are unavailable there too, for example `string.hash( ... )`.

## Prelude functions called as members

The prelude is the part of the standard library written in BoxLang. Tree-shaking removes unused functions when compiling an application. For dynamically selected functions, use `--keep name` or `--no-shaking` when needed.

## Regenerating

```bash
node tools/gen-bif-reference.mjs ../matchbox            # rewrite docs/data/functions.json and these pages
node tools/gen-bif-reference.mjs ../matchbox --check    # exit 1 when the committed files are stale
```

title: Getting Started
body: MatchBox brings BoxLang to environments where a JVM runtime is not the right fit: native applications, browsers, WASI hosts, serverless functions, and embedded devices. Start with the CLI, then select a target based on the capabilities your application needs. 1 Install MatchBox Use MVM or the direct macOS/Linux or Windows installer, or download a full CLI executable or Docker image. See installation and releases and downloads . 2 Run BoxLang Start with a script or the interactive REPL. The CLI and standalone programs do not require Java. 3 Choose a target Use the native CLI for local execution, then package for native, browser WebAssembly ( --target js ), WASI, or ESP32 as appropriate. Install Get the MatchBox CLI for your operating system and verify it works. Your first application Write a small BoxLang program, run it, and package a native executable. Agentic Development Set up a coding agent with the project context and validation loop it needs. BoxLang AI Understand how AI features in an application differ from AI-assisted development. Choose your path Native application: Start with native builds . Browser module: Read JavaScript and WebAssembly . WASI host or container: Explore experimental WASI deployment . Embedded device: Follow the ESP32 guide . Web application: Explore the webroot server or application server . MatchBox and the BoxLang JVM runtime share language concepts, but they are distinct runtimes. Check compatibility and target differences before relying on JVM libraries or host-specific APIs.

The official JVM runtime and MatchBox's independent Rust VM serve different environments and have different compatibility boundaries. THE FULL JVM ECOSYSTEM JVM BoxLang on the JVM Choose the JVM runtime when you need the broader BoxLang language and standard library, Java interoperability, or libraries and frameworks built for the Java ecosystem. Core native runtime does not require a JVM Target-specific builds for browser, WASI, and ESP32 Rust Native Fusion across all targets See compatibility and target differences → Use familiar BoxLang syntax across runtimes, and choose libraries and host APIs for the destination. ONE RUST RUNTIME, DIFFERENT TARGET PROFILES Run close to the workload Build for the host that makes sense: from a standalone desktop or server process to a browser, a WASI host, or an ESP32 device. APIs and runtime features vary by target. Native executable Bundle a MatchBox runner with compiled BoxLang bytecode. Ordinary native applications need neither Java nor a separate MatchBox install on the destination. Browser and JavaScript Ship a compiled JavaScript/WebAssembly module or use the browser runtime for dynamic BoxLang execution. WASI and containers Experiment with WebAssembly workloads in WASI hosts such as Wasmtime or WasmEdge. Filesystem and network access depend on the host. ESP32 devices Cross-compile the embedded runner for supported Xtensa and RISC-V boards. The embedded web surface is intentionally smaller than the native server. The native CLI adds a tiered Cranelift JIT that profiles hot code and compiles supported loops and functions; unsupported operations continue in the interpreter. Test reports, runtime observations, screenshots, and traces help developers and agents make the next change with evidence. Runtime introspection over MCP and browser tooling depend on the selected runtime and integration. See Agentic Development and bxPlaywright for AI agents . These projects complement BoxLang development; their integrations and runtime requirements are documented by each project. BoxLang The language and official JVM runtime. Released 2026-10-02. [GitHub release](https://github.com/ortus-boxlang/matchbox/releases/tag/v0.11.0) \| [Downloads](https://downloads.ortussolutions.com/ortussolutions/matchbox/0.11.0/)

## Added

* **Expanded BoxLang Compatibility**: Added hundreds of BIFs across arrays, structs, strings, lists, queries, sets, binary operations, encryption, conversion, decision, formatting, i18n, filesystem, JDBC, cache, system, temporal, XML, ZIP, and stream APIs.
* **Compatibility Transfer Suite**: Added more than 500 black-box tests transferred from the BoxLang JVM implementation, including operators, scopes, casters, runtime types, and global BIFs.
* **Async Runtime APIs**: Added futures, executors, thread lifecycle functions, and async collection helpers.
* **Watcher Lifecycle**: Added watcher registration, lookup, start, stop, restart, shutdown, and filesystem event dispatch.
* **System Integration**: Added native process execution, YAML deserialization, system metadata helpers, SOAP client compatibility, and raw CLI key input.
* **ESP32 HID and Web Control**: Added USB keyboard and mouse BIFs, browser-based HID controls, application configuration, diagnostics, and ESP32 examples.

## Changed

* Publish one full CLI per platform and Linux amd64/arm64 Docker images built from the same binaries.
* Follow a minor-release/development-snapshot cycle with versioned S3 downloads, evergreen channels, build metadata, and SHA-256 checksums.
* **Non-blocking HTTP**: HTTP requests now use native futures so other fibers can continue running while requests are in flight; HTTP support is enabled by default.
* **Prelude Performance**: Replaced quadratic sorting and deduplication paths with O(n log n) sorting and O(n) uniqueness checks.
* **ESP32 Memory Use**: Shared compiled route data and reduced route and HTTP caches to lower embedded memory pressure.
* **Runtime Isolation**: Watcher registries are now scoped to each VM instead of process-global state.
* **Runtime Reliability**: System output streams now flush after writes and garbage collection thresholds are configurable.

## Fixed

* Included MatchBox's default IO, HTTP, crypto, and CLI BIFs in standalone runner stubs.
* Corrected `getTempDirectory()` to preserve either path separator on every host, including Windows paths returned with `/`.
* Corrected BoxLang string parsing so backslashes remain literal and doubled quote delimiters produce one quote.
* Isolated seeded random number generators and locale settings per VM so parallel scripts cannot interfere with one another.
* Corrected BoxLang operator, tokenizer, temporal, filesystem, and cross-target compatibility behavior.
* Normalized rooted and contracted paths across platforms, validated file access modes consistently, and made watcher event path tests platform-independent.
* Added a tracked SOAP WSDL fixture so tests no longer depend on an external BoxLang checkout.
* Improved compiler and runtime error messages with more accurate source locations and context.
* Fixed ESP32 USB HID behavior and reduced route execution memory overhead.

title: MatchBox Playground
body: MatchBox Playground Run BoxLang in your browser with MatchBox compiled to WebAssembly. The page ships six demos (hello, data pipelines, Fibonacci, classes, a Mandelbrot set and the Game of Life), an editor and a stateful REPL. Code runs on your device and is never sent to a server. Limits: runs stop after 5 seconds, with 128 MiB of memory and 64 KiB for source and output. Files, network, the DOM, JVM APIs and the JIT are not available in the browser build. See differences from BoxLang and JavaScript and WebAssembly . Share and embed Copy link puts your code in the link itself, after the # , so it is never sent to a server. Anyone who opens it gets the code in their own browser and presses Run themselves. Links hold about 8 KB of compressed source. Share gives you an <iframe> for your own page, with an optional read only mode: <iframe src="https://matchbox.boxlang.io/playground/embed/#code=...&ro=true" width="600" height="400" allow="fullscreen"></iframe> Full screen expands the editor and console to the whole window. Clear empties the editor and the console, and keeps session variables.
markdown:
# MatchBox Playground

Run BoxLang in your browser with MatchBox compiled to WebAssembly. The page ships six demos (hello, data pipelines, Fibonacci, classes, a Mandelbrot set and the Game of Life), an editor and a stateful REPL. Code runs on your device and is never sent to a server.

Limits: runs stop after 5 seconds, with 128 MiB of memory and 64 KiB for source and output. Files, network, the DOM, JVM APIs and the JIT are not available in the browser build. See [differences from BoxLang](/differences-from-boxlang/index.html) and [JavaScript and WebAssembly](/building-and-deploying/javascript-and-wasm/index.html).

## Share and embed

Copy link puts your code in the link itself, after the `#`, so it is never sent to a server. Anyone who opens it gets the code in their own browser and presses Run themselves. Links hold about 8 KB of compressed source.

Share gives you an `<iframe>` for your own page, with an optional read only mode:

```html
<iframe src="https://matchbox.boxlang.io/playground/embed/#code=...&ro=true" width="600" height="400" allow="fullscreen"></iframe>
```

Full screen expands the editor and console to the whole window. Clear empties the editor and the console, and keeps session variables.

markdown:
MatchBox publishes eight full CLI binaries and a Linux multiarchitecture Docker image. See [installation](/getting-started/installation/index.html) for supported platforms and MVM commands, or [Docker](/building-and-deploying/docker-image/index.html) for image usage.

## Stable and snapshot versions

The root `Cargo.toml` holds the base version. A push to `master` releases that version, creates a stable Git tag such as `v0.11.0`, and finalizes the changelog. Stable tags are never overwritten.

After publication succeeds, CI commits the finalized changelog to `master`, advances `develop` to the next minor version, and dispatches its snapshot build. For example, releasing `0.11.0` advances development to `0.12.0`.

|        Build         | GitHub release tag | Build identity example |
|----------------------|--------------------|------------------------|
| Stable               | `v0.11.0`          | `0.11.0+42`            |
| Development snapshot | `snapshot`         | `0.12.0-snapshot+133`  |

The `+<build-number>` suffix identifies the CI build. The CLI's `--version` output also reports its source commit and build date. GitHub release titles and Docker image version labels include the build number; Git tags and Docker tags omit it.

## Download locations

[GitHub Releases](https://github.com/ortus-boxlang/matchbox/releases) and S3 publish the same platform filenames, plus `version.json` and `SHA256SUMS`.

S3 download directories are:

```text
https://downloads.ortussolutions.com/ortussolutions/matchbox/<version>/
https://downloads.ortussolutions.com/ortussolutions/matchbox/latest/
https://downloads.ortussolutions.com/ortussolutions/matchbox/snapshot/
```

Examples for Linux x64:

```text
https://downloads.ortussolutions.com/ortussolutions/matchbox/0.11.0/matchbox-linux-x64
https://downloads.ortussolutions.com/ortussolutions/matchbox/latest/matchbox-linux-x64
https://downloads.ortussolutions.com/ortussolutions/matchbox/snapshot/matchbox-linux-x64
https://downloads.ortussolutions.com/ortussolutions/matchbox/0.12.0-snapshot/matchbox-linux-x64
```

Stable version directories are immutable. The `latest` and `snapshot` channels, rolling GitHub snapshot assets, and version-keyed snapshot directories are refreshed. A path such as `0.12.0-snapshot/` is **not** an immutable build pin, and the build number is not a separate download directory. Use a stable version or Docker image digest for reproducible deployments.

## Metadata and verification

`version.json` records the base version, full build version, build ID, source revision, channel, release tag, and SHA-256 checksum for each binary. `SHA256SUMS` covers all eight binaries and `version.json`.

Download metadata/checksums from the same release or directory as the executable and verify the checksum before executing it. Linux `sha256sum`, macOS `shasum -a 256`, and Windows PowerShell `Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256` can calculate the binary's digest.

[MVM](/getting-started/installation/index.html#install-with-mvm) uses these checksums before replacing installations and compares build identity to refresh changed snapshots. It retains one rolling `snapshot` slot, not an archive of every historical snapshot build.

## Published artifacts versus source capabilities

Slim and standalone server executables are no longer published. Their source and custom build options remain available. Browser JavaScript/WASM distribution is deferred; this does not remove local browser packaging or other deployment targets. ESP32 runner publication remains disabled pending toolchain/dependency fixes; see [the ESP32 guide](/building-and-deploying/esp32/index.html) for local builds.

title: What is MatchBox?
body: MatchBox is an independent Rust implementation of the BoxLang language and runtime. It brings BoxLang to native binaries, browser and server-side WebAssembly, and embedded targets without requiring a JVM for its core runtime. BoxLang is a software productivity platform for building, modernizing, and running applications, with developers and AI agents working together. MatchBox is a pillar of that platform for workloads that need a portable runtime or a target beyond the JVM. The same language does not mean identical host APIs. markdown:
MatchBox is an independent Rust implementation of the BoxLang language and runtime. It brings BoxLang to native binaries, browser and server-side WebAssembly, and embedded targets without requiring a JVM for its core runtime.

BoxLang is a software productivity platform for building, modernizing, and running applications, with developers and AI agents working together. MatchBox is a pillar of that platform for workloads that need a portable runtime or a target beyond the JVM.

## A runtime for more places

MatchBox includes a compiler, bytecode virtual machine, command-line tools, and target-specific runners. Depending on the build and host, it can run `.bxs` scripts, package native applications, compile for JavaScript/WebAssembly in the browser, produce experimental [WASI modules and components](/building-and-deploying/wasm-container/index.html), build ESP32 applications, and serve web applications.

The same language does not mean identical host APIs. Each target has its own capabilities and constraints; review [compatibility and target differences](/differences-from-boxlang/index.html) before relying on JVM libraries or platform-specific features.

## How it fits with BoxLang

The runtimes share language concepts, while their libraries and host APIs differ. Use the JVM for Java-centric applications and MatchBox for its native, browser and embedded targets. See the [compatibility overview](/differences-from-boxlang/index.html) for guidance.

## Choose a next step

* [Install MatchBox](/getting-started/installation/index.html).
* [Build your first application](/getting-started/quick-start/index.html).
* Learn about [Agentic Development](/getting-started/agentic-development/index.html) or [BoxLang AI](/getting-started/boxlang-ai/index.html).
* Browse the [deployment targets](/index.html#targets).

markdown:
Released 2026-09-24. [GitHub release](https://github.com/ortus-boxlang/matchbox/releases/tag/v0.10.2) \| [Downloads](https://downloads.ortussolutions.com/ortussolutions/matchbox/0.10.2/)

## Added

* **Expanded BoxLang Compatibility**: Added hundreds of BIFs across arrays, structs, strings, lists, queries, sets, binary operations, encryption, conversion, decision, formatting, i18n, filesystem, JDBC, cache, system, temporal, XML, ZIP, and stream APIs.
* **Compatibility Transfer Suite**: Added more than 500 black-box tests transferred from the BoxLang JVM implementation, including operators, scopes, casters, runtime types, and global BIFs.
* **Async Runtime APIs**: Added futures, executors, thread lifecycle functions, and async collection helpers.
* **Watcher Lifecycle**: Added watcher registration, lookup, start, stop, restart, shutdown, and filesystem event dispatch.
* **System Integration**: Added native process execution, YAML deserialization, system metadata helpers, SOAP client compatibility, and raw CLI key input.
* **ESP32 HID and Web Control**: Added USB keyboard and mouse BIFs, browser-based HID controls, application configuration, diagnostics, and ESP32 examples.

## Changed

* **Non-blocking HTTP**: HTTP requests now use native futures so other fibers can continue running while requests are in flight; HTTP support is enabled by default.
* **Prelude Performance**: Replaced quadratic sorting and deduplication paths with O(n log n) sorting and O(n) uniqueness checks.
* **ESP32 Memory Use**: Shared compiled route data and reduced route and HTTP caches to lower embedded memory pressure.
* **Runtime Isolation**: Watcher registries are now scoped to each VM instead of process-global state.
* **Runtime Reliability**: System output streams now flush after writes and garbage collection thresholds are configurable.

## Fixed

* Included MatchBox's default IO, HTTP, crypto, and CLI BIFs in standalone runner stubs.
* Corrected `getTempDirectory()` to preserve either path separator on every host, including Windows paths returned with `/`.
* Corrected BoxLang string parsing so backslashes remain literal and doubled quote delimiters produce one quote.
* Isolated seeded random number generators and locale settings per VM so parallel scripts cannot interfere with one another.
* Corrected BoxLang operator, tokenizer, temporal, filesystem, and cross-target compatibility behavior.
* Normalized rooted and contracted paths across platforms, validated file access modes consistently, and made watcher event path tests platform-independent.
* Added a tracked SOAP WSDL fixture so tests no longer depend on an external BoxLang checkout.
* Improved compiler and runtime error messages with more accurate source locations and context.
* Fixed ESP32 USB HID behavior and reduced route execution memory overhead.

markdown:
MatchBox publishes one full CLI per supported operating system and architecture, with the VM, compiler, REPL, built-in webroot server, and embedded cross-platform runners. Running ordinary BoxLang code does not require a JVM.

## Install with MVM

[MatchBox Version Manager (MVM)](https://github.com/ortus-boxlang/matchbox-quick-installer) installs stable versions side by side and manages a rolling snapshot installation.

### Linux and macOS

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ortus-boxlang/matchbox-quick-installer/main/install/install.sh | bash
```

### Windows PowerShell

```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ortus-boxlang/matchbox-quick-installer/main/install/install.ps1 | iex
```

Review the installer before executing it, then follow its shell/PATH instructions and open a new terminal if needed.

### Select a MatchBox version

```sh
mvm install latest
mvm use latest
matchbox --version
```

For development builds:

```sh
mvm install snapshot
mvm use snapshot
mvm current
```

Running `mvm install snapshot` again refreshes the installation when its build ID or revision changes. Unchanged builds are skipped unless you pass `--force`. MVM keeps the `snapshot` slot, saves `version.json`, and displays the actual version, build ID, and source revision in version listings and `current`.

MVM verifies the binary's SHA-256 checksum before replacing an installation. A failed verification leaves the existing installation intact. Verification uses Linux `sha256sum`, macOS `shasum`, or Windows PowerShell `Get-FileHash`. Historical releases without `version.json` cannot be newly installed with verified-download MVM.

Use `latest` for the latest stable release, `snapshot` for the rolling development build, or a specific stable version number. Versioned snapshot names are not MVM install selectors. See [releases and downloads](/reference/releases/index.html) for channels and build identity.

## Direct CLI installation

The direct MatchBox installer prompts for stable or snapshot and installs a single CLI outside MVM's version management. Unlike MVM, these scripts do not currently verify published checksums.

### Linux and macOS

```sh
curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ortus-boxlang/matchbox/master/install/install.sh | bash
```

### Windows PowerShell

```powershell
iex (Invoke-RestMethod -Uri https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ortus-boxlang/matchbox/master/install/install.ps1)
```

These commands download and execute an installer. Review the [shell installer](https://github.com/ortus-boxlang/matchbox/blob/master/install/install.sh) or [PowerShell installer](https://github.com/ortus-boxlang/matchbox/blob/master/install/install.ps1) before running it if you prefer. Follow its PATH instructions and open a new terminal if needed.

## Verify the installation

```sh
matchbox --version
matchbox --help
matchbox
```

`--version` shows the installed version, source commit and build date (`-v` does the same).

The last command starts the REPL. Try `println("Hello from MatchBox!");`, then type `exit` or press `Ctrl+D` to leave. See the [CLI reference](/reference/cli/index.html) for every command and option.

## Published distributions

|     Distribution      |                                     Intended use                                      |
|-----------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Full CLI (`matchbox`) | Development, compilation, REPL, built-in webroot serving, and bundled target runners. |
| Docker                | The same released CLI packaged for Linux `amd64` and `arm64`.                         |

Slim and standalone server binaries are no longer published. Custom build options and the server crate remain available [from source](/getting-started/building-matchbox/index.html).

| Platform |       CLI architectures        |
|----------|--------------------------------|
| Linux    | `x64`, `x86`, `arm64`, `armv7` |
| macOS    | `x64`, `arm64`                 |
| Windows  | `x64`, `arm64`                 |

Manual downloads are individual executables named `matchbox-<os>-<arch>` (`.exe` on Windows), not release archives. Download the appropriate binary from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/ortus-boxlang/matchbox/releases) or [S3](/reference/releases/index.html#download-locations), rename it to `matchbox` or `matchbox.exe`, and add its directory to PATH. On Linux/macOS, make it executable with `chmod +x matchbox`. Verify its checksum against the same release's `SHA256SUMS` before running it.

For Docker, see [the Docker guide](/building-and-deploying/docker-image/index.html). For repeatable builds, pin a stable version or image digest rather than a moving snapshot or `latest` tag.

## Do I need Rust?

Not to run the prebuilt CLI or ordinary standalone applications. Rust is required to [build MatchBox from source](/getting-started/building-matchbox/index.html) or compile [Native Fusion](/building-and-deploying/native-fusion/index.html) code. Browser packaging without Fusion needs `wasm-bindgen` 0.2.114, not Rust; see [JavaScript and WebAssembly](/building-and-deploying/javascript-and-wasm/index.html). ESP32 builds have their own toolchain requirements; see the [ESP32 guide](/building-and-deploying/esp32/index.html).

title: Release History

body: This walkthrough uses the MatchBox CLI and a single BoxLang script. If MatchBox is not installed yet, start with Installation . markdown:
This walkthrough uses the MatchBox CLI and a single BoxLang script. If MatchBox is not installed yet, start with [Installation](/getting-started/installation/index.html).

## Write a script

Create `hello.bxs`:

```boxlang
function greet(name) {
    return "Hello, #name#!";
}

println(greet("world"));
```

## Run it

```sh
matchbox hello.bxs
```

Expected output:

```text
Hello, world!
```

MatchBox parses, compiles, and executes the file. The `.bxs` extension is used for BoxLang scripts.

## Build a standalone native executable

```sh
matchbox --target native hello.bxs
./hello
```

```text
Native binary produced: hello
Hello, world!
```

On Windows, run `hello.exe`. The output is specific to its operating system and architecture. The executable includes the MatchBox runner, so the destination does not need Java or a separate MatchBox install. See [native builds](/building-and-deploying/native-builds/index.html). Native Fusion or host integrations may introduce their own platform requirements.

## Compile portable bytecode

```sh
matchbox --build hello.bxs
matchbox hello.bxb
```

```text
Compiled to hello.bxb
Hello, world!
```

A `.bxb` file contains compiled bytecode, not a standalone runtime. Its destination still needs a compatible MatchBox runner. Keep compiler and runtime versions aligned.

To omit embedded source text:

```sh
matchbox --build --strip-source hello.bxs
```

Errors retain file and line information, but removing source reduces diagnostic context. It is not encryption or intellectual-property protection.

## Explore interactively

Start the REPL by running `matchbox` without a filename. It reads one line at a time and prints the value of an expression after `=>`. Type `exit` or `quit`, or press Ctrl+D, to leave.

```text
bx> x = 1 + 2
=> 3
bx> println(x)
3
```

Continue with [language essentials](/getting-started/features-overview/index.html), browse the [CLI reference](/reference/cli/index.html), or choose a [deployment target](/index.html#targets).

markdown:
Released 2026-08-31. [GitHub release](https://github.com/ortus-boxlang/matchbox/releases/tag/v0.10.1) \| [Downloads](https://downloads.ortussolutions.com/ortussolutions/matchbox/0.10.1/)

## Added

* **Expanded BoxLang Compatibility**: Added hundreds of BIFs across arrays, structs, strings, lists, queries, sets, binary operations, encryption, conversion, decision, formatting, i18n, filesystem, JDBC, cache, system, temporal, XML, ZIP, and stream APIs.
* **Compatibility Transfer Suite**: Added more than 500 black-box tests transferred from the BoxLang JVM implementation, including operators, scopes, casters, runtime types, and global BIFs.
* **Async Runtime APIs**: Added futures, executors, thread lifecycle functions, and async collection helpers.
* **Watcher Lifecycle**: Added watcher registration, lookup, start, stop, restart, shutdown, and filesystem event dispatch.
* **System Integration**: Added native process execution, YAML deserialization, system metadata helpers, SOAP client compatibility, and raw CLI key input.
* **ESP32 HID and Web Control**: Added USB keyboard and mouse BIFs, browser-based HID controls, application configuration, diagnostics, and ESP32 examples.

## Changed

* **Non-blocking HTTP**: HTTP requests now use native futures so other fibers can continue running while requests are in flight; HTTP support is enabled by default.
* **Prelude Performance**: Replaced quadratic sorting and deduplication paths with O(n log n) sorting and O(n) uniqueness checks.
* **ESP32 Memory Use**: Shared compiled route data and reduced route and HTTP caches to lower embedded memory pressure.
* **Runtime Isolation**: Watcher registries are now scoped to each VM instead of process-global state.
* **Runtime Reliability**: System output streams now flush after writes and garbage collection thresholds are configurable.

## Fixed

* Corrected `getTempDirectory()` to preserve either path separator on every host, including Windows paths returned with `/`.
* Corrected BoxLang string parsing so backslashes remain literal and doubled quote delimiters produce one quote.
* Isolated seeded random number generators and locale settings per VM so parallel scripts cannot interfere with one another.
* Corrected BoxLang operator, tokenizer, temporal, filesystem, and cross-target compatibility behavior.
* Normalized rooted and contracted paths across platforms, validated file access modes consistently, and made watcher event path tests platform-independent.
* Added a tracked SOAP WSDL fixture so tests no longer depend on an external BoxLang checkout.
* Improved compiler and runtime error messages with more accurate source locations and context.
* Fixed ESP32 USB HID behavior and reduced route execution memory overhead.

title: Language Essentials
body: MatchBox runs BoxLang on a Rust VM. This tour introduces the core language; use the Run buttons to try examples in your browser. For runtime and target differences, see BoxLang compatibility . For the language in depth, use the language reference . To learn by doing, start with the course . Variables, strings and operators name = "MatchBox"; active = true; count = 3; println( "Hello, #name#!" ); println( "Built with " & name ); println( count * 2 + 1 ); println( "abc" contains "b" ); println( n ?: "n is null" ); Output: Hello, MatchBox! Built with MatchBox 7 true n is null Variables are dynamically typed. & joins strings, #expression# interpolates inside a double-quoted string, and ?: supplies a value when the left side is null. See operators . Arrays and structs targets = [ "native", "browser", "embedded" ]; println( targets[ 1 ] ); targets.append( "wasi" ); println( targets.len() ); project = { name: "Hello", ready: true }; println( project.NAME ); lengths = arrayMap( targets, ( target ) => len( target ) ); println( serializeJSON( lengths ) ); { name, ready } = project; println( name & " " & ready ); println( serializeJSON( [ 0, ...targets ] ) ); Output: native 4 Hello [6,7,8,4] Hello true [0,"native","browser","embedded","wasi"] Arrays are 1-indexed and struct keys are case-insensitive. Destructuring and spread are covered in destructuring, spread and ranges . MatchBox also has a set type . Control flow and functions for ( target in [ "native", "browser" ] ) { if ( target == "native" ) { println( "Build an executable" ); } else { println( "Explore " & target ); } } switch ( "b" ) { case "a": println( "A" ); break; case "b": case "c": println( "B or C" ); break; default: println( "other" ); } function greet( name = "world" ) { return "Hello, " & name; } double = ( number ) => number * 2; println( greet() ); println( greet( name = "Ada" ) ); println( double( 21 ) ); Output: Build an executable Explore browser B or C Hello, world Hello, Ada 42 Use while , do ... while , break , continue and ranges for other loop shapes. Closures can use values from their enclosing function; see scopes . Classes class Product accessors="true" { property name; property price; function init() { return this; } } product = new Product(); product.setName( "Widget" ); println( product.getName() ); Output: Widget Use init to initialize objects and extends="Parent" to inherit behavior. See classes . Errors and asynchronous work try { throw( type = "MyError", message = "boom" ); } catch ( any e ) { println( e.type & ": " & e.message ); } finally { println( "done" ); } future = runAsync( () => { sleep( 100 ); return "finished"; } ); println( future.get() ); Output: MyError: boom done finished A typed catch handles matching errors; catch ( any e ) is a fallback. See error handling and async and futures . Function library MatchBox ships built-in functions for strings, arrays, structs, dates, JSON, regular expressions, XML, hashing and more. The function reference lists each one. Some groups are optional parts of the build: Group Needs the build feature In the browser Files and directories bif-io (default) No http() bif-http (default) Not tested, see HTTP Hashing and encryption bif-crypto (default) No ( hash is not defined) Terminal helpers bif-cli (default) No ( cliClear is not defined) Java interop bif-jni (default) No Zip and tar bif-zip Not tested Queries and datasources bif-datasource ; qoq for query of queries No See Building MatchBox for custom build options. Other parts of the language Templates (.bxm) : mix markup with BoxLang. Modules : add functions and classes with --module . Queries and data . Java interop : experimental. Native Fusion : call Rust from BoxLang.

title: Build and Run
body: MatchBox supports a quick interpreter loop and multiple deployment targets. Start by running a source file, then select a build based on the target host. Run a BoxLang script function greet(name) { return "Hello, #name#!"; } println(greet("world")); matchbox hello.bxs Use the REPL Run matchbox without a filename to start an interactive session. The prompt is bx> , each line is evaluated on its own (there is no multi-line mode, history or tab completion), and exit , quit or Ctrl+D leaves it. Build for a target matchbox --build hello.bxs # portable bytecode: Compiled to hello.bxb matchbox --target native hello.bxs # native executable: Native binary produced: hello matchbox --target js hello.bxs # ES module + WebAssembly runtime for browsers WASI targets are experimental . Cross-compilation with --target <rust-triple> needs an embedded runner for that platform. See the CLI reference and target guides , and test each artifact on its destination.
markdown:
MatchBox supports a quick interpreter loop and multiple deployment targets. Start by running a source file, then select a build based on the target host.

## Run a BoxLang script

```boxlang
function greet(name) {
    return "Hello, #name#!";
}

println(greet("world"));
```

```sh
matchbox hello.bxs
```

## Use the REPL

Run `matchbox` without a filename to start an interactive session. The prompt is `bx>`, each line is evaluated on its own (there is no multi-line mode, history or tab completion), and `exit`, `quit` or Ctrl+D leaves it.

## Build for a target

```sh
matchbox --build hello.bxs          # portable bytecode: Compiled to hello.bxb
matchbox --target native hello.bxs  # native executable: Native binary produced: hello
matchbox --target js hello.bxs      # ES module + WebAssembly runtime for browsers
```

WASI targets are [experimental](/building-and-deploying/wasm-container/index.html). Cross-compilation with `--target <rust-triple>` needs an embedded runner for that platform. See the [CLI reference](/reference/cli/index.html) and [target guides](/index.html#targets), and test each artifact on its destination.

title: Agentic Development
body: Agentic development is the practice of working with an AI coding agent that can inspect a project, make changes, and run its checks. MatchBox is one pillar of the BoxLang software productivity platform; the agent still needs clear project constraints and a way to validate its work. For BoxLang's broader approach to agentic development, see the official Agentic Development guide . Give the agent project context Add an AGENTS.md at the root of an application repository. State which MatchBox targets the application supports, how it is built and tested, and which capabilities are intentionally unavailable. Keep the guidance close to the code and update it when the project changes. The MatchBox repository includes focused skills under .agents/skills/ , including runner-development for ESP32 runner work. Skills add task-specific workflows; they do not replace checking the actual application and current MatchBox source. Keep the feedback loop executable An agent should run the same checks a developer would run and report what it could not validate. For an application, document the relevant commands, for example: matchbox --version matchbox tests/smoke.bxs matchbox --target native app.bxs The right checks depend on the target. Browser output, WASI components, and ESP32 firmware need their own runtime or toolchain validation. A successful local script run does not prove an artifact works on every target. Prefer bounded tasks Start with a behavior, target, and acceptance check. Ask the agent to inspect nearby code and relevant skills before changing files; have it show the exact commands and results afterward. Keep secrets out of prompts and test with safe local fixtures. Prompt Plan a focused MatchBox change with executable checks Copy Inspect this repository's AGENTS.md and the relevant .agents/skills before changing code. Identify the MatchBox target and existing tests for this behavior. Make the smallest change that satisfies the request, run the focused checks, and report the exact commands, results, and any target-specific behavior you could not verify. Do not claim support for a target you did not test. Separate development AI from application AI An agent helping write an application is not the same feature as an AI capability running inside that application. For the latter, see BoxLang AI . MatchBox is not a blanket guarantee that BoxLang JVM AI libraries or integrations are available; check the specific runtime and target first in compatibility and target differences .

Keep the guidance close to the code and update it when the project changes. The MatchBox repository includes focused skills under `.agents/skills/`, including `runner-development` for ESP32 runner work. Skills add task-specific workflows; they do not replace checking the actual application and current MatchBox source. ## Keep the feedback loop executable An agent should run the same checks a developer would run and report what it could not validate. For an application, document the relevant commands, for example: ```sh matchbox --version matchbox tests/smoke.bxs matchbox --target native app.bxs ``` The right checks depend on the target. Browser output, WASI components, and ESP32 firmware need their own runtime or toolchain validation. A successful local script run does not prove an artifact works on every target. ## Prefer bounded tasks Start with a behavior, target, and acceptance check. Ask the agent to inspect nearby code and relevant skills before changing files; have it show the exact commands and results afterward. Keep secrets out of prompts and test with safe local fixtures.
PromptPlan a focused MatchBox change with executable checks Inspect this repository's AGENTS.md and the relevant .agents/skills before changing code. Identify the MatchBox target and existing tests for this behavior. Make the smallest change that satisfies the request, run the focused checks, and report the exact commands, results, and any target-specific behavior you could not verify. Do not claim support for a target you did not test. ## Separate development AI from application AI An agent helping write an application is not the same feature as an AI capability running inside that application. For the latter, see [BoxLang AI](/getting-started/boxlang-ai/index.html). MatchBox is not a blanket guarantee that BoxLang JVM AI libraries or integrations are available; check the specific runtime and target first in [compatibility and target differences](/differences-from-boxlang/index.html).

title: BoxLang AI
body: BoxLang AI is about adding AI capabilities to an application: connecting providers, composing prompts, using tools and agents, and integrating capabilities such as memory or retrieval. That is different from Agentic Development , where an AI coding agent helps a developer create the application. Start with the official BoxLang AI documentation for the current feature set and supported integrations. MatchBox compatibility is target-specific MatchBox is an independent Rust runtime with its own host and target boundaries. Do not assume that a BoxLang AI module, JVM provider SDK, network client, or storage integration supported by the JVM runtime also works in MatchBox. Confirm the module's requirements and the MatchBox target's supported APIs before designing around it. For native MatchBox applications, begin with the HTTP request guide and verify the providers your application needs. Browser and embedded targets have different I/O and resource constraints; successful native behavior is not proof of browser or ESP32 support. Design for the deployment target Keep provider credentials in server-side configuration, never in browser bundles or firmware images. Use bounded timeouts, avoid logging secrets or prompts containing sensitive data, and test failure paths such as unavailable providers and malformed responses. Treat model output as untrusted input when it can influence tools or application state. For capabilities that are not documented for MatchBox, use the JVM BoxLang runtime or validate a minimal prototype on the intended MatchBox target before committing to the integration.
markdown:
BoxLang AI is about adding AI capabilities to an application: connecting providers, composing prompts, using tools and agents, and integrating capabilities such as memory or retrieval. That is different from **Agentic Development**, where an AI coding agent helps a developer create the application.

Start with the [official BoxLang AI documentation](https://boxlang.ortusbooks.com/boxlang-ai/boxlang-ai.md) for the current feature set and supported integrations.

## MatchBox compatibility is target-specific

MatchBox is an independent Rust runtime with its own host and target boundaries. Do not assume that a BoxLang AI module, JVM provider SDK, network client, or storage integration supported by the JVM runtime also works in MatchBox. Confirm the module's requirements and the MatchBox target's supported APIs before designing around it.

For native MatchBox applications, begin with the [HTTP request guide](/http/index.html) and verify the providers your application needs. Browser and embedded targets have different I/O and resource constraints; successful native behavior is not proof of browser or ESP32 support.

## Design for the deployment target

Keep provider credentials in server-side configuration, never in browser bundles or firmware images. Use bounded timeouts, avoid logging secrets or prompts containing sensitive data, and test failure paths such as unavailable providers and malformed responses. Treat model output as untrusted input when it can influence tools or application state.

For capabilities that are not documented for MatchBox, use the JVM BoxLang runtime or validate a minimal prototype on the intended MatchBox target before committing to the integration.

markdown:
Released 2026-03-18. [GitHub release](https://github.com/ortus-boxlang/matchbox/releases/tag/v0.5.0) \| [Downloads](https://downloads.ortussolutions.com/ortussolutions/matchbox/0.5.0/)

## Added

* **Built-in Web Server**: Integrated a high-performance native web server based on Axum and Tokio directly into the CLI.
* **BoxLang Markup (BXM)** : New `.bxm` template support with a pluggable transpiler that converts markup into high-speed VM bytecode.
* **Web Scopes** : Automatic injection of `url`, `form`, `cookie`, `session`, and `cgi` scopes for web requests.
* **Integrated Web CLI** : New CLI flags: `--serve`, `--port`, `--host`, and `--webroot` for instant web hosting.
* **Output Buffering** : Added request-level output buffering to the VM and a new `writeOutput()` BIF.
* **Easy Install Scripts**: One-liner installation scripts for Linux, macOS (bash), and Windows (PowerShell).
* **Multiple Release Variants**: CI now produces "Fat" (all-in-one), "Slim" (no stubs), and "Server" (headless runtime) binaries.
* **Module System** : Dynamic module discovery from `matchbox.toml` and `--module` CLI flags; new `ModuleInfo` struct encapsulating module metadata.
* **Native Module Support** : Load native Rust `.so` modules and auto-register exported BIFs without boilerplate.
* **Module Settings**: Settings support in module lifecycle hooks for configurable modules.
* **Cranelift JIT Compilation (Tier-1 \& Tier-2)**: Initial JIT backend using Cranelift. Tier-1 eliminates dead-code in empty loops; Tier-2 translates numeric loop bodies to Cranelift SSA IR.
* **JIT Type Guards and Deoptimization**: Type-checked JIT paths that fall back to the interpreter on type mismatch.
* **JIT Tier-3 --- Array Iteration** : `ArrayIterJitFn` for JIT-compiled numeric array iteration.
* **JIT Tier-3 --- Struct Inline Caching**: Per-site polymorphic shape-based caching for struct property access within JIT-compiled code, with deoptimization support.
* **JIT Hot Function Compilation and OSR**: Persistent profiling counters across quanta, fast-path execution for hot functions, and On-Stack Replacement (OSR) for long-running loops.
* **JIT Tier-4 --- Leaf Function Calls**: JIT compilation for call sites targeting leaf functions.
* **JIT Shape ID and Property Loading**: Struct property access via JIT using shape IDs and inline caches.
* **JIT String Concatenation** : JIT-compiled string concatenation via `jit_concat`.
* **JIT Enabled by Default**: JIT compilation is now active by default; no extra flag required.
* **File System BIFs** : `directoryExists`, `directoryCreate`, `directoryDelete`, `directoryList`, `fileExists`, `fileDelete`, `fileMove`, `fileCopy`, `fileInfo`, `fileCreateSymlink`, `fileSetExecutable`, `fileRead`, `fileWrite`.
* **HTTP BIF** : `httpRequest` supporting GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE methods.
* **JSON BIFs** : `jsonSerialize` and `jsonDeserialize` for encoding and decoding JSON data.
* **Cryptography BIF** : `hash` for SHA-256 hashing.
* **String BIFs** : `trim`, `listToArray`, `indexOf`, and `chr`.
* **ESP32 Firmware Support** : New `matchbox-esp32-runner` crate; CLI flags `--flash`, `--full-flash`, and `--chip` for building and flashing bytecode to ESP32 devices; watch mode for live updates during development.
* **Web WASM Target**: Stub management extended to support browser/web WASM targets alongside the existing WASM container target.
* **Elvis Operator (`?:`)**: Null-coalescing Elvis operator for concise null checks.
* **Safe Member Access (`?.`)**: Null-safe chained member access operator.
* **`while` Loop** : Full `while` loop support in the parser and compiler.
* **`switch` Statement** : `switch`/`case` statement with `break` support.

## Changed

* **Weakly Typed Math** : The `ADD` opcode now automatically converts strings to numbers if possible, matching BoxLang behavior.
* **Escaped Quote Support** : Strings now support BoxLang-style escaping using double-quotes (`""` and `''`).
* **Flat Function Representation** : Refactored `Chunk` and VM to use a flat, string-keyed function model instead of nested chunks; `CallFrame` now carries a direct chunk reference for improved dispatch.
* **Watch Mode**: Platform-specific process handling for more reliable live-reload behavior on Linux, macOS, and Windows.

## Fixed

* Fixed literal hash (`#`) parsing issues in `bxm` templates by implementing `##` escaping.
* ESP32 binary production logic and serial port handling in watch mode.
* ESP32 Docker image tagging and `Reflect.set` index usage.
* Set `RUSTUP_HOME` and `CARGO_HOME` correctly in ESP32 build environment.
* Regression in `LOCAL_JUMP_IF_NE_CONST` optimization and return propagation.

Released 2026-03-10. [GitHub release](https://github.com/ortus-boxlang/matchbox/releases/tag/v0.3.0) \| [Downloads](https://downloads.ortussolutions.com/ortussolutions/matchbox/0.3.0/)

## Added

* **System BIFs** : Added `createUUID()`, `createGUID()`, and `getSystemSetting()`.
* **CLI BIFs** : Added `cliGetArgs()` (structured parsing), `cliRead()`, `cliConfirm()`, `cliClear()`, and `cliExit()`.
* **Expanded Array Library** : 20+ new BIFs including `arraySort`, `arrayFindNoCase`, `arrayAvg`, `arraySum`, `arrayUnique`, etc.
* **Expanded Struct Library** : 15+ new BIFs including `structAppend`, `structMap`, `structFilter`, `structSort`, `structKeyExists`, etc.
* **Math BIFs** : `abs`, `min`, and `max`.
* **`rust:` Imports** : Support for importing native Rust modules and classes using `import rust:path.to.Module`.
* **MatchBox Macros** : New `matchbox-macros` crate for zero-boilerplate Rust-to-BoxLang interop (automatic BIF and Class registration).
* **Polymorphic Inline Caches (PIC)**: Enhanced member access performance with support for multiple shapes per call site.
* **Generational Garbage Collection**: Improved GC performance with young/old generation separation and optimized allocation strategies.
* **String Interning**: Added a global string interner for deduplicating identifiers and property names, reducing memory overhead.
* **Fiber Scheduling**: Implemented timeslice-based quantum management and priority handling for concurrent tasks.
* **Logical Operators** : `||`, `&&`, and unary `!` (with short-circuit evaluation).
* **Ternary Operator** : `condition ? trueValue : falseValue` expressions, nestable.
* **`continue` Statement** : Skip to the next iteration in both `for` and `for-in` loops.
* **Sparse Array Assignment** : Assigning to an out-of-bounds array index auto-grows the array, filling gaps with `null`. Reading beyond the end also returns `null` instead of throwing.
* **`--output <path>` CLI flag**: Override the output file path when compiling a script.
* **`--strip-source` CLI flag** : Strip embedded source text from compiled `.bxb` output for smaller binaries (\~35% reduction).
* **JS Interop (WASM target)** : `JsHandle`-based host function bridge (`matchbox_js_host`) for DOM and JS API access from scripts.

## Changed

* **Flat u32 Bytecode**: Refactored the entire VM to use a high-performance flat u32 opcode encoding.
* **Optimized Loop Handling** : Added specialized `FOR_LOOP_STEP` opcodes for faster iteration.
* **Generic `len()`** : The `len()` BIF now natively supports Arrays, Structs, and Strings.

## Fixed

* Fixed critical stack management bug in `CALL` where passing too many arguments caused a subtraction overflow.
* Enabled string comparison support in `GREATER` and `LESS` opcodes to allow sorting strings in prelude functions.
* Fixed deserialized function chunks causing an index-out-of-bounds panic in the VM.
* Fixed source text being duplicated into every function/method sub-chunk at compile time.
* `continue` now works correctly inside `for-in` loops.

Released 2026-03-07. [GitHub release](https://github.com/ortus-boxlang/matchbox/releases/tag/v0.2.0) \| [Downloads](https://downloads.ortussolutions.com/ortussolutions/matchbox/0.2.0/)

## Added

* **BoxLang-Authored Prelude** : Standard BIFs (e.g., `arrayMap`, `structEach`, `arrayFilter`, `isEmpty`) are now implemented in BoxLang, reducing core VM size.
* **Tree-Shaking Compiler**: Automated dependency analysis to exclude unused prelude functions from standalone binaries.
* **Cross-Compilation Support** : Embedded runner stubs for Linux, macOS, and Windows into "fat" CLI binaries via the `cross-compile` Cargo feature.
* **Multi-Stage CI**: Refactored GitHub Actions to natively build stubs on each OS and aggregate them into single distribution binaries.
* **Namespaced Function Attributes** : Support for `@matchbox-keep` to explicitly preserve symbols from tree-shaking.
* **New CLI Flags** :
  * `--keep <symbols>`: Manually preserve BIFs in the final binary.
  * `--no-shaking`: Disable tree-shaking to include the full prelude.
  * `--no-std-lib`: Completely exclude the standard library.
* **Java Interop**: Implemented dynamic JNI reflection bridge for automatic Java method discovery and invocation.
* **Asynchronous Execution** : Implemented `runAsync` BIF and VM-level fiber spawning.
* **Documentation** : Added comprehensive documentation structure in `/docs`.

## Changed

* Migrated multiple BIFs (Math, Array, Struct) from Rust implementations to the BoxLang prelude.
* Refactored `build.rs` to support pre-existing stub injection and multi-target compilation.
* Unified bytecode serialization to `u32` for better cross-platform compatibility.

## Fixed

* Fixed specialized integer math opcodes (`OpAddInt`, `OpSubInt`, `OpMulInt`) to correctly handle float-backed constants.
* Resolved grammar conflict between classic for-loop initialization and optional semicolons.
* Fixed case-insensitivity in member method resolution (e.g., `.toUpperCase()` correctly maps to `ucase`).

* Member method delegation to BIFs (e.g., `"foo".ucase()`).
* High-performance integration testing macro.
* GitHub Actions for automated multi-platform builds.
* Tracing Mark-and-Sweep Garbage Collector.
* Hidden Classes (Shapes) and Monomorphic Inline Caches for performance.

## Changed

* Renamed project from `bx-rust` to `MatchBox`.
