Key Concepts Concept Where to look BoxLang state/actions todo.bxs Generated browser namespace todo.js → window.MatchBox.modules["todo"] Readiness signal window.MatchBox.ready("todo") Generic state helper window.MatchBox.State("todo", ...) in index.html Alpine store wiring index.html
markdown:
A minimal browser Todo application written in BoxLang and compiled to WebAssembly.
BoxLang owns the app state and state transitions. The HTML shell wires that
state into Alpine using the generated `window.MatchBox.State(...)` helper.

## Project Layout

    wasm_browser/
    ├── todo.bxs    ← BoxLang source (state + DOM rendering logic)
    └── index.html  ← HTML shell (imports the compiled ES module)

## How It Works

`matchbox --target js` compiles `todo.bxs` to an **ES module** (`todo.js` + `todo.wasm`).

* **BoxLang owns the state** and returns plain snapshot structs for the UI.
* **The generated browser contract owns readiness and module lookup** through `window.MatchBox`.
* **The page owns framework wiring** by creating an Alpine store from `window.MatchBox.State("todo", ...)`.

## Build

You need the `matchbox` binary and the `wasm-bindgen` command-line tool on your `PATH` (`cargo install wasm-bindgen-cli`, or set `WASM_BINDGEN` to its path). `wasm-pack` is not used.

```bash
cd docs/examples/wasm_browser
matchbox --target js todo.bxs
```

This produces these files alongside your source:

    todo.js               ← ES module wrapper (import this in HTML)
    todo.wasm             ← WebAssembly binary (loaded automatically by todo.js)
    todo.d.ts             ← TypeScript declarations
    todo_bg.wasm.d.ts     ← TypeScript declarations for the wasm exports

## Run Locally

Browsers block WASM loading over `file://` for security reasons. Serve the
directory with any local HTTP server:

```bash
# Option A - Node.js (npx, no install required)
npx serve .

# Option B - Python
python3 -m http.server 8080

# Option C - any other static file server
```

Then open the printed URL (usually `http://localhost:3000` or
`http://localhost:8080`) in your browser.

## Features

* Add a task by typing in the input and pressing **Enter** or clicking **Add**.
* Click a task text to toggle it **done / undone**.
* Click **✕** to remove a task.

## Deploy to Production

The compiled output (`todo.js`, `todo.wasm` and `index.html`) is a fully static
bundle. Upload it to any static host:

```bash
# Vercel
vercel deploy

# Netlify drag-and-drop
# Upload the wasm_browser/ folder to app.netlify.com/drop
```

Ensure your server sets the correct MIME type for `.wasm` files:

    Content-Type: application/wasm

Most modern hosts (Netlify, Vercel, Cloudflare Pages) handle this automatically.

## Key Concepts

|           Concept           |                    Where to look                     |
|-----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
| BoxLang state/actions       | `todo.bxs`                                           |
| Generated browser namespace | `todo.js` → `window.MatchBox.modules["todo"]`        |
| Readiness signal            | `window.MatchBox.ready("todo")`                      |
| Generic state helper        | `window.MatchBox.State("todo", ...)` in `index.html` |
| Alpine store wiring         | `index.html`                                         |

title: Web server
body: MatchBox has two web runtimes. Both are implemented in the matchbox_server crate and run on the same VM as the CLI. Webroot server App server Start with matchbox --serve matchbox_server --app app.bxs Routing The file path in the URL Routes you register in a script Pages .bxm and .bxs templates plus static files Handlers, middleware, event.setView() templates Configuration boxlang.json in the webroot Calls in the script ( app.listen() ) WebSockets Yes, through boxlang.json Yes, through app.enableWebSockets() Example Web server App server , WebSocket counter Webroot server matchbox --serve --webroot ./site --port 8080 Flag Default Meaning --webroot <dir> . Directory to serve. --port <n> 8080 Listen port. --host <addr> 127.0.0.1 Bind address. Use 0.0.0.0 to accept connections from other machines, for example inside a container. matchbox --serve accepts only these three flags and reads boxlang.json from the webroot. The --config <file> flag exists only on the matchbox_server binary, which you build from the MatchBox source tree with cargo build --release -p matchbox_server . On startup the server prints the address, the resolved webroot and whether rewrites are enabled. Files are read on every request, so edits appear without a restart. What gets served Request Result A .bxm or .bxs file Rendered as a template. Response is 200 with Content-Type: text/html and a MBX_SESSION_ID cookie. Any other file Sent as is, with a content type guessed from the extension. A directory index.bxm , then index.bxs , inside it. A missing file 404 Not Found , or the rewrite file when rewrites are on. A path with a segment that starts with . 403 . A path that climbs out of the webroot 403 . A method other than GET , HEAD or POST 405 with allow: GET,HEAD,POST . HEAD returns the headers of the GET response with an empty body. A template that throws returns 500 with the error text. Scopes in templates Scope Contents url Query-string parameters. form Fields of an application/x-www-form-urlencoded POST body. JSON bodies are not exposed. cookie Request cookies, plus MBX_SESSION_ID . session A struct kept in server memory per MBX_SESSION_ID cookie. cgi request_method , script_name , path_info , server_name , server_port , http_host , content_type , content_length . It is not the process environment. All values are strings. Session values are stored as strings between requests, so a number or struct you assign comes back as its string form on the next request. Sessions have no expiry and are lost when the process stops. To read an environment variable use getSystemSetting( "NAME", "default" ) . There is no env scope. boxlang.json Place boxlang.json in the webroot. All keys are optional. { "rewrites": true, "rewriteFileName": "index.bxm", "websocket": { "uri": "/ws", "listenerClass": "Chat", "listenerState": { "greeting": "hello" }, "handler": "WebSocket.bx" } } Key Default Meaning rewrites false When true , a request whose file does not exist is answered by rewriteFileName instead of a 404. The original path is available as cgi.path_info , and the query string stays in url . This applies to every missing file, including missing images and stylesheets. rewriteFileName index.bxm Front-controller file, relative to the webroot. A value that contains .. or starts with / is replaced by the default. websocket none Enables a WebSocket endpoint. See below. If boxlang.json is not valid JSON, or a websocket block is missing one of uri , listenerClass or listenerState , the whole file is ignored without a warning and the defaults apply. Check the "Rewrites:" line printed at startup. Give each directory an index template; directory requests do not fall back to the rewrite file. WebSockets in the webroot server The websocket block names a class and the file that defines it. Key Meaning uri Path that accepts WebSocket upgrades. listenerClass Name of the class to instantiate. listenerState JSON object. Its keys are set as instance variables of the listener ( variables.greeting ). The constructor is not called. handler File that defines the class. Default WebSocket.bx . It is looked up case-insensitively in the webroot directory itself, not in subdirectories. class Chat { function onConnect( channel ) { channel.sendJson( { "welcome": variables.greeting, "id": channel.getId() } ); } function onMessage( message, channel ) { channel.broadcastMessage( "echo:" & message ); } function onClose( channel ) {} } If the handler file is missing or does not compile, the server starts without a WebSocket endpoint. An error thrown in onConnect or onMessage is printed on the server's stderr and closes that connection with code 1011. WebSocket channel API The same channel object is passed to listeners in both server modes. Method Purpose sendMessage( text ) , sendText( text ) Send a text frame to this client. sendJson( value ) Serialize value as JSON and send it as text. sendBytes( bytes ) Send a binary frame. broadcastMessage( text ) , broadcastText( text ) Text frame to every connected client, including this one. broadcastJson( value ) , broadcastBytes( bytes ) The same for JSON and binary payloads. close( [code], [reason] ) Close the connection. Default code 1000 . getId() Server-generated UUID of this connection. getPath() Path of the upgrade request, such as /ws . getURL() Full URL of the upgrade request, including the query string. getHTTPHeader( name, [default] ) Header of the upgrade request. Names are matched case-insensitively. Returns null when missing and no default is given. Listener hooks are onConnect( channel ) , onMessage( message, channel ) and onClose( channel ) . message is a string for text frames and bytes for binary frames. The channel has no properties: channel.id is null , use getId() . App server The app server runs one script that builds a routed application with web.server() . It is started with the --app flag of the matchbox_server binary: cargo run -p matchbox_server -- --app app.bxs matchbox app.bxs cannot run such a script: the CLI does not install the web namespace, and web.server() fails with Method server not found on null . In --app mode the --port , --host , --webroot and --config flags are ignored; the address comes from app.listen() . import boxlang.web; app = web.server(); app.get( "/hello/:name", function( event, rc, prc ) { event.renderJson( { "message": "Hello " & rc.name } ); } ); app.listen( 8090 ); The script is compiled once at startup and is not reloaded when the file changes. Its top level runs at startup and then again on every request, in a fresh VM, so variables set at the top of the script do not carry over between requests. Keep shared state in session , a file or a database. Application object Call Purpose app.get/post/put/patch/delete( path, [middleware...], handler ) Register a route. app.use( middleware ) Add middleware that runs for every request. app.group( prefix ) Returns a group with the same methods, a path prefix and its own use() . Groups nest. app.middleware.buildStaticFiles( mount, dir ) Middleware that serves files from dir (relative to the script) under mount . Missing files fall through to routing. app.webhook( builder, handler ) , app.buildWebhook() Signed webhook endpoint. See below. app.enableWebSockets( uri, listener ) Attach a listener object. Its state is snapshotted when you register it. app.listen( port ) or app.listen( { host, port } ) Where to listen. Default 127.0.0.1:8080 . Routes: A path segment that starts with : captures that segment. There are no wildcards or regular expressions. A route matches only when the number of segments is equal. The first registered match wins. Only get , post , put , patch and delete can be registered. Other methods get 404 . An unmatched request returns 404 with the text Not Found . Middleware has the signature function( event, rc, prc, next ) and continues the chain with next.run() . Handlers have the signature function( event, rc, prc ) . Request collections Name Contents rc Query parameters, then form fields, then top-level keys of a JSON body, then route parameters. A later source overwrites an earlier one with the same name. prc Private collection for passing data between middleware and handlers. session Per-session struct, keyed by the MBX_SESSION_ID cookie that the server sets. The store is in memory, round-trips through JSON (only JSON types survive), and has no expiry. JSON bodies are parsed when Content-Type is JSON. The server does not limit the request body size. markdown:
MatchBox has two web runtimes. Both are implemented in the `matchbox_server` crate and run on the same VM as the CLI.

|               | Webroot server                                       | App server                                                                                                               |
|:--------------|:-----------------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Start with    | `matchbox --serve`                                   | `matchbox_server --app app.bxs`                                                                                          |
| Routing       | The file path in the URL                             | Routes you register in a script                                                                                          |
| Pages         | `.bxm` and `.bxs` templates plus static files        | Handlers, middleware, `event.setView()` templates                                                                        |
| Configuration | `boxlang.json` in the webroot                        | Calls in the script (`app.listen()`)                                                                                     |
| WebSockets    | Yes, through `boxlang.json`                          | Yes, through `app.enableWebSockets()`                                                                                    |
| Example       | [Web server](/examples/web_server/README/index.html) | [App server](/examples/app_server/README/index.html), [WebSocket counter](/examples/websocket_counter/README/index.html) |

## Webroot server

```sh
matchbox --serve --webroot ./site --port 8080
```

| Flag              | Default     | Meaning                                                                                                |
|:------------------|:------------|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `--webroot <dir>` | `.`         | Directory to serve.                                                                                    |
| `--port <n>`      | `8080`      | Listen port.                                                                                           |
| `--host <addr>`   | `127.0.0.1` | Bind address. Use `0.0.0.0` to accept connections from other machines, for example inside a container. |

`matchbox --serve` accepts only these three flags and reads `boxlang.json` from the webroot. The `--config <file>` flag exists only on the `matchbox_server` binary, which you build from the MatchBox source tree with `cargo build --release -p matchbox_server`.

On startup the server prints the address, the resolved webroot and whether rewrites are enabled. Files are read on every request, so edits appear without a restart.

### What gets served

| Request                                     | Result                                                                                                  |
|:--------------------------------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| A `.bxm` or `.bxs` file                     | Rendered as a template. Response is `200` with `Content-Type: text/html` and a `MBX_SESSION_ID` cookie. |
| Any other file                              | Sent as is, with a content type guessed from the extension.                                             |
| A directory                                 | `index.bxm`, then `index.bxs`, inside it.                                                               |
| A missing file                              | `404 Not Found`, or the rewrite file when rewrites are on.                                              |
| A path with a segment that starts with `.`  | `403`.                                                                                                  |
| A path that climbs out of the webroot       | `403`.                                                                                                  |
| A method other than `GET`, `HEAD` or `POST` | `405` with `allow: GET,HEAD,POST`.                                                                      |

`HEAD` returns the headers of the `GET` response with an empty body. A template that throws returns `500` with the error text.

### Scopes in templates

| Scope     | Contents                                                                                                                                                      |
|:----------|:--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `url`     | Query-string parameters.                                                                                                                                      |
| `form`    | Fields of an `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` POST body. JSON bodies are not exposed.                                                                      |
| `cookie`  | Request cookies, plus `MBX_SESSION_ID`.                                                                                                                       |
| `session` | A struct kept in server memory per `MBX_SESSION_ID` cookie.                                                                                                   |
| `cgi`     | `request_method`, `script_name`, `path_info`, `server_name`, `server_port`, `http_host`, `content_type`, `content_length`. It is not the process environment. |

All values are strings. Session values are stored as strings between requests, so a number or struct you assign comes back as its string form on the next request. Sessions have no expiry and are lost when the process stops.

To read an environment variable use `getSystemSetting( "NAME", "default" )`. There is no `env` scope.

### boxlang.json

Place `boxlang.json` in the webroot. All keys are optional.

```json
{
  "rewrites": true,
  "rewriteFileName": "index.bxm",
  "websocket": {
    "uri": "/ws",
    "listenerClass": "Chat",
    "listenerState": { "greeting": "hello" },
    "handler": "WebSocket.bx"
  }
}
```

| Key               | Default     | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|:------------------|:------------|:--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `rewrites`        | `false`     | When `true`, a request whose file does not exist is answered by `rewriteFileName` instead of a 404. The original path is available as `cgi.path_info`, and the query string stays in `url`. This applies to every missing file, including missing images and stylesheets. |
| `rewriteFileName` | `index.bxm` | Front-controller file, relative to the webroot. A value that contains `..` or starts with `/` is replaced by the default.                                                                                                                                                 |
| `websocket`       | none        | Enables a WebSocket endpoint. See below.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

If `boxlang.json` is not valid JSON, or a `websocket` block is missing one of `uri`, `listenerClass` or `listenerState`, the whole file is ignored without a warning and the defaults apply. Check the "Rewrites:" line printed at startup.

Give each directory an index template; directory requests do not fall back to the rewrite file.

### WebSockets in the webroot server

The `websocket` block names a class and the file that defines it.

| Key             | Meaning                                                                                                                                         |
|:----------------|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `uri`           | Path that accepts WebSocket upgrades.                                                                                                           |
| `listenerClass` | Name of the class to instantiate.                                                                                                               |
| `listenerState` | JSON object. Its keys are set as instance variables of the listener (`variables.greeting`). The constructor is not called.                      |
| `handler`       | File that defines the class. Default `WebSocket.bx`. It is looked up case-insensitively in the webroot directory itself, not in subdirectories. |

    class Chat {
        function onConnect( channel ) {
            channel.sendJson( { "welcome": variables.greeting, "id": channel.getId() } );
        }

        function onMessage( message, channel ) {
            channel.broadcastMessage( "echo:" & message );
        }

        function onClose( channel ) {}
    }

If the handler file is missing or does not compile, the server starts without a WebSocket endpoint. An error thrown in `onConnect` or `onMessage` is printed on the server's stderr and closes that connection with code 1011.

## WebSocket channel API

The same `channel` object is passed to listeners in both server modes.

| Method                                              | Purpose                                                                                                                   |
|:----------------------------------------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `sendMessage( text )`, `sendText( text )`           | Send a text frame to this client.                                                                                         |
| `sendJson( value )`                                 | Serialize `value` as JSON and send it as text.                                                                            |
| `sendBytes( bytes )`                                | Send a binary frame.                                                                                                      |
| `broadcastMessage( text )`, `broadcastText( text )` | Text frame to every connected client, including this one.                                                                 |
| `broadcastJson( value )`, `broadcastBytes( bytes )` | The same for JSON and binary payloads.                                                                                    |
| `close( [code], [reason] )`                         | Close the connection. Default code `1000`.                                                                                |
| `getId()`                                           | Server-generated UUID of this connection.                                                                                 |
| `getPath()`                                         | Path of the upgrade request, such as `/ws`.                                                                               |
| `getURL()`                                          | Full URL of the upgrade request, including the query string.                                                              |
| `getHTTPHeader( name, [default] )`                  | Header of the upgrade request. Names are matched case-insensitively. Returns `null` when missing and no default is given. |

Listener hooks are `onConnect( channel )`, `onMessage( message, channel )` and `onClose( channel )`. `message` is a string for text frames and bytes for binary frames. The channel has no properties: `channel.id` is `null`, use `getId()`.

## App server

The app server runs one script that builds a routed application with `web.server()`. It is started with the `--app` flag of the `matchbox_server` binary:

```sh
cargo run -p matchbox_server -- --app app.bxs
```

`matchbox app.bxs` cannot run such a script: the CLI does not install the `web` namespace, and `web.server()` fails with `Method server not found on null`. In `--app` mode the `--port`, `--host`, `--webroot` and `--config` flags are ignored; the address comes from `app.listen()`.

    import boxlang.web;

    app = web.server();

    app.get( "/hello/:name", function( event, rc, prc ) {
        event.renderJson( { "message": "Hello " & rc.name } );
    } );

    app.listen( 8090 );

The script is compiled once at startup and is not reloaded when the file changes. Its top level runs at startup and then again on every request, in a fresh VM, so variables set at the top of the script do not carry over between requests. Keep shared state in `session`, a file or a database.

### Application object

| Call                                                              | Purpose                                                                                                                |
|:------------------------------------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `app.get/post/put/patch/delete( path, [middleware...], handler )` | Register a route.                                                                                                      |
| `app.use( middleware )`                                           | Add middleware that runs for every request.                                                                            |
| `app.group( prefix )`                                             | Returns a group with the same methods, a path prefix and its own `use()`. Groups nest.                                 |
| `app.middleware.buildStaticFiles( mount, dir )`                   | Middleware that serves files from `dir` (relative to the script) under `mount`. Missing files fall through to routing. |
| `app.webhook( builder, handler )`, `app.buildWebhook()`           | Signed webhook endpoint. See below.                                                                                    |
| `app.enableWebSockets( uri, listener )`                           | Attach a listener object. Its state is snapshotted when you register it.                                               |
| `app.listen( port )` or `app.listen( { host, port } )`            | Where to listen. Default `127.0.0.1:8080`.                                                                             |

Routes:

* A path segment that starts with `:` captures that segment. There are no wildcards or regular expressions.
* A route matches only when the number of segments is equal. The first registered match wins.
* Only `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch` and `delete` can be registered. Other methods get `404`.
* An unmatched request returns `404` with the text `Not Found`.

Middleware has the signature `function( event, rc, prc, next )` and continues the chain with `next.run()`. Handlers have the signature `function( event, rc, prc )`.

### Request collections

| Name      | Contents                                                                                                                                                                      |
|:----------|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `rc`      | Query parameters, then form fields, then top-level keys of a JSON body, then route parameters. A later source overwrites an earlier one with the same name.                   |
| `prc`     | Private collection for passing data between middleware and handlers.                                                                                                          |
| `session` | Per-session struct, keyed by the `MBX_SESSION_ID` cookie that the server sets. The store is in memory, round-trips through JSON (only JSON types survive), and has no expiry. |

JSON bodies are parsed when `Content-Type` is JSON. The server does not limit the request body size.

### The event object

| Method                                                                                                 | Returns or does                                                                                                              |
|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `getCollection()`, `getPrivateCollection()`, `getSession()`                                            | The `rc`, `prc` and `session` structs.                                                                                       |
| `valueExists( key )`, `privateValueExists( key )`, `sessionExists( key )`                              | Whether the key exists.                                                                                                      |
| `getValue( key, [default] )`, `getPrivateValue( key, [default] )`, `getSessionValue( key, [default] )` | Read a value.                                                                                                                |
| `setValue( key, value, [private=false] )`                                                              | Set a value in `rc`, or in `prc` when the third argument is true.                                                            |
| `paramValue( key, default )`, `paramPrivateValue( key, default )`, `paramSessionValue( key, default )` | Set the value only when the key is missing. `setSessionValue` is an alias of `paramSessionValue`.                            |
| `getOnly( keys )`, `getExcept( keys )`                                                                 | A struct holding only, or everything but, the named keys of `rc`.                                                            |
| `getRouteParams()`                                                                                     | Struct of the `:name` captures.                                                                                              |
| `getCurrentRoute()`                                                                                    | The matched pattern, such as `/hello/:name`.                                                                                 |
| `getHTTPMethod()`, `getRequestMethod()`                                                                | The request method.                                                                                                          |
| `getPath( [withQuery=true] )`                                                                          | Request path, with the raw query string unless `false`.                                                                      |
| `getURL( [withQuery=true] )`                                                                           | Full request URL, or only the path when `false`.                                                                             |
| `getHTTPHeader( name, [default] )`                                                                     | Request header. Names are case-insensitive.                                                                                  |
| `getHTTPCookie( name, [default] )`, `getCookie`                                                        | Request cookie.                                                                                                              |
| `isJSON()`, `isAjax()`                                                                                 | Whether the request has a JSON content type, or `X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest`.                                          |
| `getHTTPContent( [asJson=false] )`                                                                     | Raw body as a string, or parsed JSON when `true`. Invalid JSON gives a `400`.                                                |
| `setHTTPHeader( name, value )`                                                                         | Add a response header.                                                                                                       |
| `setHTTPCookie( name, value, [path="/"], [httpOnly=false] )`, `setCookie`                              | Add a `Set-Cookie` header.                                                                                                   |
| `setHTTPStatus( code )`                                                                                | Set the response status.                                                                                                     |
| `clearSession()`, `invalidateSession()`                                                                | Empty the session struct.                                                                                                    |
| `renderText( text )`, `renderHTML( html )`, `renderJSON( value )`                                      | Set the body and content type.                                                                                               |
| `renderData( "json" \| "html" \| "text" \| "plain", data )`                                            | Same, with the format as an argument.                                                                                        |
| `setView( path, [viewArgs] )`, `renderTemplate( path, [viewArgs] )`                                    | Render a `.bxm` template (relative to the script) as HTML. The template sees `event`, `rc`, `prc`, `session` and `viewArgs`. |

`renderJSON` writes numbers as floating point, so `1` is serialized as `1.0`.

### Errors

If a handler throws, the response status comes from the start of the error message:

| Message contains | Status |
|:-----------------|:-------|
| `Bad Request:`   | `400`  |
| `Unauthorized:`  | `401`  |
| `Conflict:`      | `409`  |
| anything else    | `500`  |

The body is the error text, or `{"error": "..."}` when the request sends `Accept: application/json`.

### Webhooks

    app.webhook(
        app.buildWebhook()
            .path( "/webhooks/stripe" )
            .secret( getSystemSetting( "STRIPE_SECRET" ) )
            .signatureHeader( "stripe-signature" )
            .prefix( "sha256=" )
            .timestampHeader( "stripe-timestamp" )
            .toleranceSeconds( 300 )
            .replayHeader( "stripe-event-id" )
            .replayTtlSeconds( 300 ),
        function( event, rc, prc ) {
            event.renderText( "ok" );
        }
    );

A webhook is a `POST` route. The server computes an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body with the secret and compares its lowercase hex form with the signature header, after removing `prefix` if the header starts with it. A bare hex signature is also accepted.

| Builder method                           | Rule                                                                                                                                   |
|:-----------------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `path`, `secret`, `signatureHeader`      | Required.                                                                                                                              |
| `prefix`                                 | Optional text stripped from the header value.                                                                                          |
| `timestampHeader` and `toleranceSeconds` | Set both or neither. The header must hold Unix seconds within the tolerance of the server clock. The timestamp is checked, not signed. |
| `replayHeader`                           | Delivery id header. A repeated id for the same path is rejected with `409` for the TTL.                                                |
| `replayTtlSeconds`                       | Requires `replayHeader`. Default `3600`. The replay store is in memory.                                                                |

A missing or wrong signature, a missing or stale timestamp, or a missing delivery id returns `401`.

### WebSockets in the app server

    listener = new ClickCounterSocket();
    listener.configure();
    app.enableWebSockets( "/ws", listener );

The listener and the channel API are the same as in the webroot server, except that the listener is an instance you create and configure yourself. Its state is captured when `enableWebSockets()` is called and restored inside the WebSocket runtime.

markdown:
This example serves a directory with `matchbox --serve`. It has BoxLang Markup (`.bxm`) pages, a static CSS file, and the `url`, `form`, `cookie`, `session` and `cgi` scopes. The [Web server guide](/building-and-deploying/web-server/index.html) covers the server in full.

## Project structure

* `index.bxm`: Home page. Counts visits in the **session** and prints the time.
* `about.bxm`: Prints `cgi.server_port`.
* `contact.bxm`: Reads `url.name` and shows the session id from the **cookie** scope.
* `styles.css`: A static file, served as `text/css`.

## How it works

Every `.bxm` or `.bxs` file under the webroot is rendered as a template when you request it. Other files are sent as they are. A request for a directory is answered by its `index.bxm` or `index.bxs`.

Each page render starts with these scopes:

* `url`: query-string parameters.
* `form`: fields of a URL-encoded POST body.
* `cookie`: request cookies, including `MBX_SESSION_ID`.
* `session`: a struct held in server memory for each `MBX_SESSION_ID` cookie. Values are kept as strings.
* `cgi`: `request_method`, `script_name`, `path_info`, `server_name`, `server_port`, `http_host`, `content_type` and `content_length`.

The server is built on Axum and Tokio and runs the same VM as the `matchbox` command.

## Running the example

1. From the `docs/examples` directory of the MatchBox source tree, or any directory that contains a copy of `web_server`:

   ```bash
   matchbox --serve --webroot web_server --port 8080
   ```

2. Open `http://localhost:8080`.
3. Visit `http://localhost:8080/contact.bxm?name=MatchBox` to see URL parameter handling.
4. Reload the home page. The visit count in `session.visitCount` goes up each time your browser sends the same session cookie.

The server listens on `127.0.0.1` unless you pass `--host 0.0.0.0`.
> \[!note\] Template tags
> Use `<bx:output>` to evaluate `#expression#` in markup. This example keeps branching in `<bx:script>` and renders the result with one output block.

markdown:
This example demonstrates the routed app server plus SocketBox-style websocket listeners.

It serves an HTML page at `/`, opens a websocket connection to `/ws`, increments a shared counter when the button is clicked, and broadcasts the new count to every connected browser tab.

## Project Structure

* `app.bxs`: Main routed app plus websocket listener registration.
* `views/home.bxm`: HTML page with the client-side websocket code.

## Key Concepts

### 1. Listener Class Registration

WebSockets are enabled with a listener instance:

```boxlang
import boxlang.web;

listener = new ClickCounterSocket();
listener.configure();

app.enableWebSockets( "/ws", listener );
```

MatchBox snapshots the listener instance state when you register it, then restores that state inside the websocket runtime. This keeps preconfigured listener objects usable instead of forcing a zero-argument constructor.

### 2. Listener Lifecycle

The listener class uses the familiar SocketBox-style methods:

* `onConnect( channel )`
* `onMessage( message, channel )`
* `onClose( channel )`

### 3. Channel Helpers

The `channel` object currently supports:

* `sendMessage()` / `sendText()`
* `sendJson()`
* `sendBytes()`
* `broadcastMessage()` / `broadcastText()`
* `broadcastJson()`
* `broadcastBytes()`
* `close()`
* `getId()`, `getPath()`, `getURL()` and `getHTTPHeader( name, [default] )`, which describe the connection and its upgrade request

The [Web server guide](/building-and-deploying/web-server/index.html#websocket-channel-api) describes each method. This example uses `sendJson()` to initialize new connections and `broadcastJson()` to fan out counter changes.

## Running the Example

The `--app` flag belongs to the `matchbox_server` binary, which you build from the MatchBox source tree. From the project root:

```bash
cargo run -p matchbox_server -- --app docs/examples/websocket_counter/app.bxs
```

Then open:

* `http://localhost:8099/`

Open the page in two tabs and click the button in either tab. Both tabs update to the same counter value. The count lives in the listener inside the WebSocket runtime, so it survives page reloads and resets when the server restarts.

To attach a listener without a routed app, use the `websocket` block of `boxlang.json` in a webroot; see the guide.

title: Welcome to MatchBox
body: BoxLang is a dynamic language for building applications. It normally runs on the JVM. MatchBox is a second runtime for the same language, written in Rust. markdown:
**BoxLang** is a dynamic language for building applications. It normally runs on the JVM. **MatchBox** is a second runtime for the same language, written in Rust. It compiles your code to bytecode and runs it on a small virtual machine, which lets BoxLang go places the JVM does not fit: a single native executable, a browser tab, a serverless function, even a microcontroller.

You write the same language either way. What changes is where it runs and what you can reach from it. MatchBox complements the JVM runtime, it does not replace it. See [what is MatchBox](/getting-started/what-is-matchbox/index.html) and [differences from BoxLang](/differences-from-boxlang/index.html) for the details.

## Your first script

Press **Run this in your browser** under the code. Nothing is installed and nothing is sent to a server: the compiler and the VM run on your device.

```boxlang
function greet( name ) {
    return "Hello, #name#!";
}

println( greet( "MatchBox" ) );
```

Output:

```text
Hello, MatchBox!
```

A few things to notice:

* `.bxs` is the file extension for a BoxLang **script**.
* `#name#` inside a double-quoted string inserts the value of `name`. You will see more of this in lesson 3.
* `println` writes a line to the console.

## Try it

Change `"MatchBox"` to your own name and run it again. Then add a second `println` call that greets someone else.

## Choose a target

Native, browser, WASI and ESP32 applications use the same language with different host APIs and resources. Start with a small project on the target you want to use. The [compatibility overview](/differences-from-boxlang/index.html) helps you choose.

## Keep going

You finished the course. Thank you for learning MatchBox. The fastest way to get better now is to build something small and real: a script that reads your own data, a tiny web page, or a command-line tool. Come back to the [playground](/playground/index.html) any time you want to test an idea.
